questions.answer: The pressure on the bottom face is greater than the pressure on the top face because the bottom is deeper. The corresponding upward pressure force is therefore greater than the downward pressure force, while appropriate sideways forces cancel, so the resultant is upward.
accepted_alternatives: An explanation in terms of a greater bottom pressure force and cancellation of horizontal forces.

marking_points.text: States that pressure, and hence pressure force for equal face area, is greater on the deeper bottom face than on the top face.
Explains that the unequal vertical pressure forces give an upward resultant, with appropriate sideways forces cancelling.

option_feedback.A: Greater absolute pressure is not enough. Both top and bottom pressures rise, while the pressure difference and displaced volume stay unchanged.
option_feedback.B: Distance from the surface does not reduce upthrust for a rigid object fully submerged in a uniform liquid.
option_feedback.C: Correct. F = ρgV is unchanged because ρ, g and the displaced volume V are unchanged.
option_feedback.D: Upthrust equals weight only when the full vertical force balance requires it, such as for free floating equilibrium.

marking_points.text: Selects C: the upthrust stays constant because fluid density and displaced volume stay constant.

option_feedback.A: Changing the liquid does not change the block's weight.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Floating equilibrium still requires the same upthrust, so a denser fluid needs a smaller displaced volume.
option_feedback.C: The block's total volume is unchanged, but only its submerged volume sets the displaced volume.
option_feedback.D: At rest with no other vertical force, the upthrust equals the weight, not a greater value.

marking_points.text: Selects B: the block displaces a smaller volume because denser fluid supports the same weight.

option_feedback.A: This subtracts the density ratio from 100% instead of using the ratio itself.
option_feedback.B: Correct. The submerged fraction is ρ_object/ρ_fluid = 650/1000 = 0.65.
option_feedback.C: A solid less dense than the liquid can float with only part of its volume submerged.
option_feedback.D: This reverses the density ratio and gives an impossible submerged fraction greater than the whole object.

questions.unit_policy: Accept 65% or option B; percentage has no unit.

marking_points.text: Selects B: 65% of the solid's volume is submerged.
Calculates the fully displaced volume as (0.40)(0.25)(0.18) = 0.0180 m³.

parts.answer: F = ρgV = (1000)(9.81)(0.0180) = 176.58 N, so F = 177 N upward to three significant figures.
parts.unit_policy: N required; upward direction may be stated here or understood from upthrust.

marking_points.text: Uses F = ρgV with water density 1000 kg m⁻³ and displaced volume 0.0180 m³.
Obtains an upthrust of 177 N upward to three significant figures.

parts.answer: For equilibrium, T + F = W. T = 250 - 176.58 = 73.42 N, so the cable tension on the case is 73.4 N upward.

marking_points.text: Uses vertical equilibrium as tension plus upthrust equals the 250 N weight.
Obtains a cable tension of 73.4 N acting upward on the case.

parts.answer: Weight acts downward and upthrust acts upward. Since the float is freely floating at rest, their magnitudes are equal.
accepted_alternatives: F = W with the correct force directions.

marking_points.text: Identifies weight downward and upthrust upward as the two vertical forces.
States that upthrust equals weight because the freely floating cylinder is in equilibrium.

parts.answer: ρ_oil gV = mg, so V = m/ρ_oil = 48/800 = 0.0600 m³.

marking_points.text: Equates ρ_oil gV to mg for floating equilibrium and rearranges for V.
Obtains a displaced oil volume of 0.0600 m³.
Uses h = V/A to obtain a submerged depth of 0.300 m in oil.

parts.answer: In water, V = 48/1000 = 0.0480 m³ and h = 0.0480/0.20 = 0.240 m. Water is denser, so each cubic metre displaced has greater weight and a smaller volume is needed to support the same float weight.
accepted_alternatives: 0.24 m with an explanation based on greater fluid density and smaller required displaced volume.

marking_points.text: Calculates the new submerged depth as 0.240 m in water.
Explains that denser water requires a smaller displaced volume to provide the same upthrust equal to the fixed weight.

parts.answer: The bottom face is deeper, so its pressure and upward pressure force are greater than the top face's pressure and downward force. Sideways forces cancel, leaving an upward resultant.

marking_points.text: States that the deeper bottom face has greater pressure and pressure force than the top face.
